figures.finding: A child is a person under fifteen; no child may work in an industrial undertaking, and from thirteen children may be employed in non-industrial establishments, but one who hasn't completed Form III may not work in a place of public entertainment except for non-profit purposes. For the development of art or training the Commissioner for Labour may permit the employment of child entertainers of any age by special permission, applied for in writing before work begins: for extras (Form CEF-1 and the script or storyboard) at least two working days ahead, for contract artistes (CEF-1, CEF-2, the child's employment record, the parent's written consent and a school attendance certificate or proof of Form III) at least seven. The standard conditions: no work before 7 a.m. or after 11 p.m.; at most eight hours a day, four on a school day in term, none in school hours; at most four days a week and, in term, three from Monday to Saturday; twelve hours' rest after each day's work; a break of an hour after five hours (and a further half hour for a child under six); free transport home after 7 p.m.; nothing dangerous to life, health or morals. Unpaid cultural performances need only a notice (Form CEF-6) fourteen days ahead, at most seven days a month or four a week. The permission is for entertainers, so it doesn't name a child writer or director, who falls under the general Regulations (reading).

value.permit: special permission of the Commissioner for Labour

figures.applies: Employment of Children Regulations (Cap. 57B) as the Labour Department applies them.

sources.said: A “child” is defined under the Employment Ordinance as a person under the age of 15 years. ... No person shall employ a child in any industrial undertaking. Subject to certain restrictions in the Employment of Children Regulations, children aged 13 or over may be employed in non-industrial establishments. However, children of this category, who have not completed Form III of secondary education, are forbidden to enter into employment in any place of public entertainment except for non-profit making purposes. ... For the development of art or training, the Commissioner for Labour may permit the employment of children of different ages as entertainers by granting exemption from certain provisions of the Employment of Children Regulations. ... The application (Form CEF-1) should reach the Labour Department at least 2 working days before commencement of the employment. ... should reach the Labour Department at least 7 working days before commencement of the employment.

(i) No child shall be employed • before 7 a.m. or after 11 p.m.; • for a period of employment more than 8 hours on any day; • for working more than 4 hours on school day during the school term; • during school hours; • for more than 4 days in a week and during school term for more than 3 days from Monday to Saturday; • during the 12 hours immediately following the ending of his work on any day; and • to work continuously for more than 5 hours without a break of not less than 1hour for a meal or rest and, in the case of a child under the age of 6, without an additional rest period of not less than half an hour within the said spell of 5 hours. (ii) Free transport should be provided to take each child employee home if he is required to work after 7 p.m. ... the frequency of performances does not exceed seven days per month or four days per week.

figures.finding: The Film Development Fund's Production Financing Scheme 2.0 accepts only a film production company registered under the Companies Ordinance (or a registered non-Hong Kong company), and every director of the film must be a Hong Kong permanent resident; it sets no age, so a young producer applies through a company (see companies).

value.applicant: film production company registered under Cap. 622

sources.said: 4.2.1 The Applicant must be a film production company which is (i) a Hong Kong company formed and registered under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) ... 4.3.4 All Film Director(s) of the Film Project must be permanent resident(s) in Hong Kong.
